Indian Standard
SPECIFICATION FOR VEGETABLE FIBRE BASE JOINTING MATERIAL 0. FOREWORD
0.1
This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 29 January 1970, after the draft finalized by the Gaskets and Packings Sectional Committee had, been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. The vegetable fibre base jointing material covered bi this standard is suitable for use at temperatures not exceeding 120�C in system involving contact with mineral or di-ester type lubricating oil, mineral oil type hydraulic fluid and petroleum fuel. It is not recommended for use with water based fluids.

03

0.3 Jointing conforming to this standard is resistant to deleterious attack by mould growth under tropical storage conditions and is suitable for commercial and defence purposes. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with The number of significant places retained in the rounded off IS : 2-1960'. value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements of compressible vegetable fibre base jointing material in the form of sheets from which gaskets can be cut or stamped. 2. MATERIAL AND MANUFACTURE

2.1 The finished material shall consist of one or more plies of paper impregnated with plasticized gelatine which is subsequently rendered insoluble with formaldehyde. The plasticizer shall be glycerine or a +&&a fgr roundii

The glycerine shall be of technical grade quality complying with the requirements of IS : 1796-l 960*. 2.1.1 The paper shall not contain mechanical wood. During manufacture a s.uitable fungicide shall be incorporated to render finished material resistant to mould growth. The composition of fungicide shall be as agreed to between the. manufacturer and purchaser. 2.2 The cracking, material shall be capable of being tearing or separation of the plies. material shall be normally cut supplied or punched the the the the

The thickness shall be determined at 10 points evenly distributed across the width of the sheets at right angles to the machine direction of the material. Measurements shall be made to the nearest 0.01 mm using the grade 2 micrometer having an anvil of not less than 10 mm diameter ( see IS : 2967-1964* ). 6.1.2 Tensile StrengthThe tensile strength of the material when determined by the method described in 12.3 of IS : 1060 ( Part 1 )-1966t shall be not less than 120 kgf/cms in either the machine or the cross direction. 6.1.3 Comfxessibility and Compression Set - The compressibility and compression set of the material when determined by the method described in Appendix B shall be as follows: Compressibility Compression Set 25 to 35 percent 12.5 percent, Max

6.2.1 These shall be conducted whenever there is a change in the basic composition of the jointing material and shallconstitute (a) flexibility, and (b) resistance to mould growth. 6.2.2 Flexibili& - The flexibility of the material shall be such that, when tested by the method described in Appendix F, the test pieces shall not crack or separate into layers. 6.2.3 Resistance to Mould Growth- The material when tested as described in Appendix G shall have no visible mould growth on any part of the test pieces. 7. MARKING 7.1 A minimum of every 1 000 ems of the material shall be marked on one side only with the manufacturer's name, nominal thickness and any other marking as specified by the purchaser. 7.1.1 Mark. The material may also be marked with the IS1 Certification

NOTE - The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act, and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard, under a well-defined system of inspection, testin Thii system, which is devised and super vise! and quality control during production. by IS1 and operated by the producer, has the further safeguard that the products as actually marketed are continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to the standard. Details of conditions, under which a licence for the use of the ISI Certification Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processon, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

APPENDIX ( Clause 6.1.3 )
METHOD FOR

B

DETERMINATION OF COMPRESSIBILITY AND COMPRESSION SET

B-l.

APPARATUS

E-1.1 The test shall be carried out on a suitable compression testing machine fitted with smooth steel platens of diameter not less than 50 mm so that their faces remain parallel to each other throughout the test, The load shall be applied normally to the faces of the platens. B-l.2 The compressibility of the material shall two dial indicators graduated in millimetres and shall be rigidly attached to the upper loading the diameter, with their spindles resting on the datum level. l&2. TEST SPECIMENS be measured by means of accurate to 2.5 tirn which platen at opposite ends of lower platen or other flxed I

B-2.1 The specimens circular in shape and of area 5 cm* shall be punched from the sample with a sharp die. For samples of thickness 1.60 mm and above, twenty such specimens shall be cut. For sample thicknesses~ between 0.80 mm and 1.60 mm, forty such specimens shall be cut and from these a composite specimen for testing shall be prepared by pairing together two specimens selected at random without the use of adhesive.

ls : 5!%6 - 1970 B-2.2, Materials
the practical of thickness less than 0.80 mm cannot be tested difficulty in making satisfactory measurement. owing to

B-3. CONDITIONING shall be dried over silica gel for not less than 18 hours and then exposed to an atmosphere of 65 f 2 percent relative humidity and 27O f 2�C. Five of the specimens shall be weighed to an accuracy of 0901 gram immediately and at 24.hour intervals thereafter. The specimens must show a gain in weight after the first 24 hours period and when they show ndther gain nor loss in weight exceeding one percent in each of two consecutive 24 hours periods, all the specimens may be considered to hake reached equilibrium and testing may begin. Where it is not possible to carry out the compression testing in a conditioned room, the samples shall be removed from the conditioning atmosphere one at a time and transported to the test apparatus in a sealed container and tested immediately. Norm-The conditioning of spccim~~~ must be strictly in accordance with the procedure laid down as it is known that departure from this in any way may materially affect the subsequent results. B-4. METHOD OF DETERMIN ATION OF JIG YIELD \

B-3.1 The specimens

B-4.1 The jig yield is defined as the deflection of the apparatus caused by the increase from the pre-load to the major load. This jig yield shall be determined immediately prior to each series of tests adopting the following procedure without the insertion of test specimens:
Apply pre-load of 35 kgf and maintain this for two minutes before recording the mean dial gauge readings (Jo). Increase the load at a steady rate to the--major load of 450 kgf and maintain this for two minutes before recording the mean dial gauge readings (Jr). Reduce the load to the pre-load of 35 kgf and maintain this for 30 seconds before recording the mean dial gauge readings us). The jig yield J = J1 - Je.
NOTE-If the values ofJa and 3, difliz by more than 5 gm, the apparatus ir showing non-elastic yield and is not in a suitable condition for carrying out the tsta.

A sufficient number of such determinations shall be made until the maximum and minimum of five consecutive determinations do not differ by more than 7 Pm. The mean of these five values shall constitute jig yield of the apparatus. B5. place

METHOD OF TEST
and the mean of 35 kgf shall be applied with no test specimen in of the two dial gauge readings (I,) shall be recorded. 8

B-5.1 The pm-load

IS : 5566 - 1970 The procedure shall be repeated with the specimens placed centrally between the platens and this load maintained constant for two minutes. The mean of the two dial gauge readings (&) shall be reccrded. The load shall then be increased at a steady rate over a period of 20 to 30 seconds to the major load of 450 kgf. This'load shall be maintained for two minutes when the mean of the two dial gauge readings (Ts) shall again be recorded. The total load shall then be removed and the sample allowed to recover for two minutes in the free state. The pre-load of 35 kgf shall then be reapplied and after 30 seconds under this load the mean of the two dial gauge readings (T's) shall again be recorded. Twenty determinations shall be carried out on each batch of material. B-6. RESULTS B-6.1 The results shall be calculated to the nearest 0.1 percent as follows: Compressibility = ( G - Ts) -J ( G - T0 ) G) 100 2-0) 100 percent

APPENDIX

D

( Clauses 6.151, 6.1.5.2 and 6.1.5.3 )
METHOD OF TESTING FOR FREEDOM FROM CORROSIVE IMPURITIES D-l. PREPARATION OF WATER EXTRACT - The extraction apparatus shall consist of a 500-ml borosilicate glass flask, to which is attached by means of a ground glass joint an efficient reflux condenser, fitted with a guard tube with a suitable reagent forthe exclusion of carbon dioxide and atmospheric impurities.
D-l.2 Procedure D-1.2.1 Cut out a portion of the sample of material into pieces about 6 mma_,weigh about 10 g into the flask and add to this test portion 20 times Fit the reflux condenser and guard its weight of demineralized water. tube, heat the water to boiling point and continue boiling gently for one hour. Replace the reflux condenser by a stopper and guard tube and cool to room temperature.

D-l.1 Apparatus

D-1.2.2 Immediately before preparing the water extract, boil abou 100 ml of the demineralized water in the apparatus for one hour. Stopper the flask and cool. The apparatus shall be considered to be satisfactory of the water is not greater than if the electrical conductivity 2 micromhosjcm.
NOTE- In order to comply with the above requirement, it will normally be necessary to use demineralized water having an electrical conductivity not greater than 1 micromho/cm.

D-2, DETERMINATION OF pH VALUE OF WATER EXTRACT D-2.1 A portion of the water extract of the material shall be decanted into
a suitable cell and the /JH value determined in accordance with 10 of The determination shall be made as soon as IS : 1060 ( Part I )-1966*. the water extract has cooled to room temperature. The cell shall be rinsed with the demineralized water immediately before using. OF CHLORIDE AND SULPHATE

D-3. DETERMINA'FION CONTENTS

D-3.1 A suitable aliquot portion equivalent to W grams of sample of the extract prepared according to D-l shall be taken and evaporated to nearly

APPENDIX ( Clause 6.2.2 )
METHOD F-l. TEST PIECES

F

OF TEST FOR FLEXIBILITY

F-l.1 The test pieces used shall be strips 12 mm wide and 100 to 125 mm long, of which three shall be cut from the sample in the machine direction and three in the cross direction. They shall be conditioned at 27" js 2�C

14

Is : 5566 - 1970 and 65 f 2 percent before the test. F-2. PROCEDURE relative humidity for at least 18 hours immediately

F-2.1 Each test piece shall be bent through 180" round a cylindrical mandrel having a diameter equal to five times the nominal thickness of the material. The time of bending shall be approximately 2 seconds and the test piece will be maintained in the bent position for 10 seconds.

PROCEDURE G3.I Each test piece shall be inoculated with a fine spray of the mixed aqueous spore suspension as described in G2, care being taken not to saturate the material with water.
